title: Adaptive sampling probe for tail-latency detection + prioritized rollback
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds an adaptive sampling probe that improves sensitivity to tail-latency regressions and a prioritized rollback policy to reduce blast radius. No API contract changes for public endpoints; rollout behind feature flag.
description: Background: Some recent canary signals were missed because fixed-rate sampling under-represented rare slow-paths (long-context requests, batched spikes, cache warmups). This PR introduces an adaptive-sampling probe and a complementary prioritized rollback policy to make continuous perf monitoring more robust. Goals: 1) increase detection sensitivity for Q99/Q99.9 regressions without increasing overall metric cost; 2) enable progressive rollback that reduces user-visible impact by demoting newer variants first and protecting high-priority routes. Changes in this PR: - New component: perf/probes/adaptive_sampler implements reservoir+variance-driven sampling. It monitors per-route tail-latency windows and automatically increases sample rate up to sampling.max_rate when tail-variance exceeds hysteresis thresholds, and decays back to sampling.min_rate when stable. - New detector: tail_latency_q99_9_drift which uses multi-window smoothing (1m/5m/30m) and empirical bayes smoothing to reduce false positives on transient spikes. - Rollout policy: rollout/prioritized_rollback supports a priority map (route -> priority integer). When a detector trips, the rollout controller will first pull traffic from lower priority routes/variants before global rollbacks. This is configurable via rollout.priority_map and rollout.scale_step. - Config + persistence: adds perf_probe.enabled flag and probe configuration persisted in metadata store (probe_configs table). Backwards compatible: default off in main; no behavior change until enabled. - Observability: adds Grafana dashboard panel perf-probe-tail-latency-v2 and Alert: ProbeHighTailLatency (thresholds defaulted to conservative values). - Tests: unit tests for reservoir sampler and end-to-end canary integration test using canary-emulator traffic harness. - Docs: internal runbook for prioritized rollback and example YAML for tuning sampling.min_rate/max_rate. Checklist: - [x] design review (ENG-15433) - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration test with canary-emulator - [x] basic dashboard + alert - [x] feature-flag gating - [x] docs/runbook updated Rollout plan: Stage 1: merge behind feature flag, enable on perf-canary staging for 48h and monitor ProbeHighTailLatency and existing canary signals. Stage 2: enable on a subset of routes (low priority) in prod for 72h. Stage 3: widen to more routes and tune thresholds. Implementation notes: sampling.min_rate defaults to 0.005 (0.5%), max_rate defaults to 0.20 (20%). Reservoir sampler uses per-route reservoir size 1024 for stable tail estimates. The detector uses QN estimator with exponential decay to prefer recent behavior. See linked tests for evaluation graphs. Related: builds on earlier work around canary windows and drift smoothing but takes a different approach by changing sampling to actively surface rare slow events.

notes_for_release: Feature gated behind perf_probe.enabled=false by default. Enable in staging via: `redwoodctl config set perf_probe.enabled true` and tune sampling.{min_rate,max_rate} per route. Recommended to run for 72h on a small subset before broad rollout.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased sampling could add CPU/metrics cost. Mitigation: upper bound with sampling.max_rate and route-level opt-out.
Risk: False positives on transient spikes. Mitigation: multi-window smoothing + conservative default thresholds and staged rollout.
Risk: Behavioral change in canary signal processing. Mitigation: feature-flagged and requires explicit enable; integration tests exercise end-to-end behavior.
